decisions.reason: The verb means to assess what is said and tell what comes from God (m1). Literal says "juzgar"; Balanced "evaluar", the word used for assessing in 2:14. "Discernir" is kept for the gift of 12:10, and "examinar" for a different verb (verse 24; 4:3).

decisions.choice: wapime
decisions.reason: "Kupima" (weigh, test) is assessing what is said to tell what comes from God (meaning decision), as the English "weigh"; "kuhukumu" (judge) would suggest condemning.

decisions.choice: "분별하다" (L, B) for weighing, the verb of "분별함" in 12:10
decisions.reason: The meaning decision ties the verb to the gift of distinguishing spirits; Korean keeps the same root.

decisions.choice: avaliem
decisions.reason: "Avaliar" is to weigh and assess, not to condemn (m1); "julgar" would suggest passing judgment on the prophets.

source.text: ἐὰν δὲ ἄλλῳ ἀποκαλυφθῇ καθημένῳ, ὁ πρῶτος σιγάτω.

records.literal_gloss: If but to another it is revealed sitting, the first let be silent.

en.L: But if [something] is revealed to another who is sitting [there], let the first be silent.
en.B: And if something is revealed to another person who is sitting there, the first speaker should keep silent.
en.R: If God shows something to another person who is sitting there, the first prophet should be silent and let that person speak.

fr.L: Mais si [quelque chose] est révélé à un autre qui est assis [là], que le premier se taise.
fr.B: Et si quelque chose est révélé à un autre qui est assis là, le premier doit se taire.
fr.R: Si Dieu montre quelque chose à une autre personne assise là, le premier prophète doit se taire et la laisser parler.

es.L: Pero si a otro que está sentado le es revelado [algo], que el primero calle.
es.B: Y si a otro que está sentado allí se le revela algo, el primero debe guardar silencio.
es.R: Si Dios le muestra algo a otra persona que está sentada allí, el primer profeta debe callar y dejar hablar a esa persona.

sw.L: Lakini [kitu] kikifunuliwa kwa mwingine aliyeketi [hapo], wa kwanza na anyamaze.
sw.B: Na ikiwa jambo fulani limefunuliwa kwa mtu mwingine aliyeketi hapo, msemaji wa kwanza anyamaze.
sw.R: Ikiwa Mungu anamwonyesha jambo mtu mwingine aliyeketi pale, nabii wa kwanza anyamaze na kumwachia mtu huyo aseme.

vi.L: Nhưng nếu [điều gì] được bày tỏ cho một người khác đang ngồi [đó], thì người thứ nhất hãy im lặng.
vi.B: Và nếu có điều gì được bày tỏ cho một người khác đang ngồi đó, thì người đang nói trước nên im lặng.
vi.R: Nếu Đức Chúa Trời cho một người khác đang ngồi đó thấy một điều gì, thì nhà tiên tri thứ nhất nên im lặng để người kia nói.

ko.L: 그러나 앉아 있는 다른 사람에게 [무엇이] 계시되면, 먼저 [말하던] 사람은 잠잠하십시오.
ko.B: 그러나 앉아 있는 다른 사람에게 무엇이 계시되면, 먼저 말하던 사람은 잠잠히 있으십시오.
ko.R: 하나님께서 거기 앉아 있는 다른 사람에게 무엇을 보여 주시면, 먼저 예언하던 사람은 말을 멈추고 그 사람이 말하게 하십시오.

pt.L: Mas, se [algo] for revelado a outro que está sentado, o primeiro fique em silêncio.
pt.B: E, se alguma coisa for revelada a outra pessoa que está sentada ali, quem estava falando primeiro deve ficar em silêncio.
pt.R: Se Deus mostrar alguma coisa a outra pessoa que está sentada ali, o primeiro profeta deve ficar em silêncio e deixar essa pessoa falar.

decisions.choice: is revealed: God gives a revelation
decisions.reason: ἀποκαλυφθῇ is passive, with God as the one who reveals (2:10). This is the 'revelation' of verses 6 and 26, given to a prophet.

decisions.choice: sitting: the hearers sat while the one speaking stood
decisions.reason: A speaker could stand to address a gathering (Acts 13:16); here the others are seated. The word marks the person as one of the hearers.

decisions.choice: be silent: the first prophet stops, to let the other speak
decisions.reason: The same verb as in verses 28 and 34. Here it means giving way, as verse 31 explains: all can prophesy in turn.

decisions.choice: God shows; and let that person speak
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one who reveals (m1) and says why the first prophet is silent (m3).

decisions.choice: be silent (L, R); keep silent (B)
decisions.reason: As in verse 28.

source.text: δύνασθε γὰρ καθ’ ἕνα πάντες προφητεύειν, ἵνα πάντες μανθάνωσιν καὶ πάντες παρακαλῶνται καὶ πνεύματα προφητῶν προφήταις ὑποτάσσεται, οὐ γάρ ἐστιν ἀκαταστασίας ὁ θεὸς ἀλλὰ εἰρήνης, ὡς ἐν πάσαις ταῖς ἐκκλησίαις τῶν ἁγίων.

records.literal_gloss: You are able for one by one all to prophesy, so that all may learn and all may be encouraged \v 32 and spirits of prophets to prophets are subject, \v 33 not for is of disorder the God but of peace, as in all the churches of the holy ones.

en.L: For you are all able to prophesy one at a time, so that all may learn and all may be encouraged; \v 32 and prophets' spirits are subject to prophets, \v 33 for God is [the God] not of disorder but of peace, as in all the churches of the holy ones.
en.B: You can all prophesy, each in turn, so that all of you learn and all of you are encouraged. \v 32 Prophets have their own spirits under their control. \v 33 God is the God of peace, not of disorder, as is true in all the churches of God's holy people.
en.R: All of you can prophesy, one at a time, so that everyone can learn and everyone can be encouraged. \v 32 Prophets can control themselves when they prophesy. \v 33 God does not cause confusion. He brings peace. That is true in all the churches of God's people.

fr.L: Car vous pouvez tous prophétiser un par un, afin que tous apprennent et que tous soient encouragés ; \v 32 et les esprits des prophètes sont soumis aux prophètes, \v 33 car Dieu n’est pas [un Dieu] de désordre, mais de paix, comme dans toutes les églises des saints.
fr.B: Vous pouvez tous prophétiser, chacun à son tour, pour que tous apprennent et que tous soient encouragés. \v 32 Les prophètes gardent la maîtrise de leur propre esprit. \v 33 Dieu est un Dieu de paix, non de désordre ; il en est ainsi dans toutes les églises du peuple saint de Dieu.
fr.R: Vous pouvez tous prophétiser, l’un après l’autre, pour que tout le monde apprenne et que tout le monde soit encouragé. \v 32 Les prophètes peuvent se contrôler quand ils prophétisent. \v 33 Dieu ne provoque pas le désordre. Il apporte la paix. C’est ainsi dans toutes les églises du peuple de Dieu.

es.L: Porque todos {{plural_you:pueden|podéis}} profetizar uno por uno, para que todos aprendan y todos sean animados; \v 32 y los espíritus de los profetas están sujetos a los profetas, \v 33 porque Dios no es [Dios] de desorden sino de paz, como en todas las iglesias de los santos.
es.B: Todos {{plural_you:pueden|podéis}} profetizar, cada uno a su turno, para que todos aprendan y todos reciban ánimo. \v 32 Los profetas tienen dominio sobre su propio espíritu. \v 33 Dios es Dios de paz, no de desorden, como sucede en todas las iglesias del pueblo santo de Dios.
es.R: Todos {{plural_you:ustedes pueden|vosotros podéis}} profetizar, uno por uno, para que todos puedan aprender y todos reciban ánimo. \v 32 Los profetas pueden controlarse cuando profetizan. \v 33 Dios no causa confusión. Él trae paz. Así es en todas las iglesias del pueblo de Dios.

sw.L: Kwa maana nyote mnaweza kutabiri mmoja mmoja, ili wote wajifunze na wote watiwe moyo; \v 32 na roho za manabii ziko chini ya manabii, \v 33 kwa maana Mungu si [Mungu] wa machafuko bali wa amani, kama katika makanisa yote ya watakatifu.
sw.B: Nyote mnaweza kutabiri, kila mmoja kwa zamu yake, ili nyote mjifunze na nyote mtiwe moyo. \v 32 Manabii wanazitawala roho zao wenyewe. \v 33 Mungu ni Mungu wa amani, si wa machafuko, kama ilivyo katika makanisa yote ya watu watakatifu wa Mungu.
sw.R: Nyote mnaweza kutabiri, mmoja baada ya mwingine, ili kila mtu ajifunze na kila mtu atiwe moyo. \v 32 Manabii wanaweza kujitawala wanapotabiri. \v 33 Mungu haleti machafuko. Yeye huleta amani. Ndivyo ilivyo katika makanisa yote ya watu wa Mungu.

vi.L: Vì tất cả anh chị em đều có thể lần lượt từng người nói tiên tri, để mọi người đều học hỏi và mọi người đều được khích lệ; \v 32 và tâm linh của các nhà tiên tri phục dưới các nhà tiên tri, \v 33 vì Đức Chúa Trời không phải [là Đức Chúa Trời] của sự hỗn loạn nhưng của sự bình an, như trong tất cả các Hội Thánh của các thánh đồ.
vi.B: Tất cả anh chị em đều có thể lần lượt nói tiên tri, để mọi người đều học hỏi và mọi người đều được khích lệ. \v 32 Các nhà tiên tri làm chủ được tâm linh của chính mình. \v 33 Đức Chúa Trời là Đức Chúa Trời của sự bình an, chứ không phải của sự hỗn loạn, như trong tất cả các Hội Thánh của dân thánh Đức Chúa Trời.
vi.R: Tất cả anh chị em đều có thể nói tiên tri, lần lượt từng người một, để mọi người đều học được và mọi người đều được khích lệ. \v 32 Các nhà tiên tri có thể tự kiềm chế mình khi nói tiên tri. \v 33 Đức Chúa Trời không gây ra sự hỗn loạn. Ngài đem lại bình an. Điều đó đúng trong tất cả các Hội Thánh của dân Đức Chúa Trời.

ko.L: 여러분은 모두 한 사람씩 예언할 수 있습니다. 모두가 배우고 모두가 권면을 받게 하려는 것입니다. \v 32 예언하는 사람들의 영은 예언하는 사람들에게 복종합니다. \v 33 하나님은 무질서의 하나님이 아니시고 평화의 [하나님]이시기 때문입니다. 성도들의 모든 교회에서와 같이 [그러합니다].
ko.B: 여러분은 모두 차례대로 한 사람씩 예언할 수 있습니다. 그래서 모두가 배우고 모두가 권면을 받을 수 있습니다. \v 32 예언하는 사람은 자기 영을 스스로 다스릴 수 있습니다. \v 33 하나님은 무질서의 하나님이 아니시고 평화의 하나님이십니다. 성도들의 모든 교회에서도 그렇습니다.
ko.R: 여러분 모두가 한 사람씩 차례로 예언할 수 있습니다. 그러면 모든 사람이 배우고 모든 사람이 용기를 얻을 수 있습니다. \v 32 예언하는 사람은 예언할 때 자기 자신을 다스릴 수 있습니다. \v 33 하나님께서는 혼란을 일으키시는 분이 아니십니다. 평화를 주시는 분이십니다. 하나님의 백성의 모든 교회에서도 그렇습니다.

pt.L: Pois todos vocês podem profetizar um por um, para que todos aprendam e todos sejam encorajados; \v 32 e os espíritos dos profetas estão sujeitos aos profetas, \v 33 pois Deus não é [Deus] de desordem, mas de paz, como em todas as igrejas dos santos.
pt.B: Todos vocês podem profetizar, cada um na sua vez, para que todos aprendam e todos sejam encorajados. \v 32 Os profetas têm o próprio espírito sob controle. \v 33 Deus é o Deus da paz, não da desordem, como acontece em todas as igrejas do povo santo de Deus.
pt.R: Todos vocês podem profetizar, um de cada vez, para que todos possam aprender e todos possam ser encorajados. \v 32 Os profetas conseguem se controlar quando profetizam. \v 33 Deus não causa confusão. Ele traz paz. É assim em todas as igrejas do povo de Deus.

decisions.choice: you can all prophesy one by one: there is room for every prophet to speak, in turn
decisions.reason: ἕνα with the preposition before it means one at a time. πάντες probably means all who have the gift of prophecy, not every believer (12:29: not all are prophets).

decisions.choice: be encouraged: be urged on and strengthened
decisions.reason: παρακαλῶνται is the verb related to 'encouragement' in verse 3.

decisions.choice: the spirits of prophets are subject to prophets: prophets can control their own inspired speech, and so can wait their turn
alternatives: what one prophet says is subject to the assessment of the other prophets (verse 29)
decisions.reason: πνεύματα προφητῶν are the prophets' own spirits as God's Spirit moves them, as with 'my spirit' in verse 14. Prophecy does not seize a person against their will, so a prophet can stop to let another speak (verse 30). Others read the words with verse 29: what one prophet says is subject to the others who weigh it.

decisions.choice: God is not a God of disorder but of peace: the way the church meets should reflect who God is
decisions.reason: ἀκαταστασίας is disorder, unrest (2 Corinthians 12:20). God is the God of peace (Romans 15:33; 16:20; Philippians 4:9), and a gathering where all speak at once does not show him.

decisions.choice: as in all the churches of the holy ones: belongs with what comes before, closing Paul's teaching on orderly speaking
alternatives: begins the next sentence: 'As in all the churches of the holy ones, let the women be silent in the churches'
decisions.reason: Ancient manuscripts have little punctuation, so where the phrase belongs is an editorial judgment. The SBLGNT puts a comma before it and a full stop after it, so that it ends Paul's teaching on orderly speaking; Paul ends other instructions with an appeal to what all the churches do (4:17; 7:17; 11:16). Others join it to verse 34, which would then begin 'As in all the churches'; but that sentence goes on to say 'in the churches' again.

decisions.choice: the holy ones: God's people, set apart for him
decisions.reason: As in 1:2 and 6:1-2, ἁγίων are all believers, not a special class.

decisions.choice: Prophets have their own spirits under their control (B); Prophets can control themselves when they prophesy (R)
alternatives: the spirits of prophets are subject to prophets
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable follow m3. Literal keeps the Greek wording, which can be read either way.

decisions.choice: God's holy people (B); God's people (R)
decisions.reason: As in Philippians and Colossians; Literal says 'the holy ones'.

decisions.choice: God is the God of peace, not of disorder
alternatives: God is not a God of disorder but of peace
decisions.reason: Balanced puts the positive statement first.

decisions.choice: les saints (L); le peuple saint de Dieu (B); le peuple de Dieu (R)
decisions.reason: As in Colossians (style guide 9): in modern French "les saints" suggests believers of exceptional holiness, while Paul means all of God's people, set apart for him (m6).

decisions.choice: los santos (L); el pueblo santo de Dios (B); el pueblo de Dios (R)
decisions.reason: As in 1:2 and 6:1-2.

decisions.choice: roho za manabii (lowercase)
decisions.reason: The prophets' own spirits, their inspired speech, which they can control (meaning decision, footnoted), so "roho" is lowercase with the agreement of things ("ziko"), as in verse 14.

decisions.choice: "평화의 하나님" (L, B); "평화를 주시는 분" (R)
decisions.reason: The words of Romans 15:33 and 16:20 for the God of peace.

decisions.choice: "as in all the churches of the holy ones" ends verse 33, closing the teaching on orderly speaking
decisions.reason: The meaning decision follows the SBLGNT, which joins the phrase to what comes before; the other reading is footnoted.

source.text: Αἱ γυναῖκες ἐν ταῖς ἐκκλησίαις σιγάτωσαν, οὐ γὰρ ἐπιτρέπεται αὐταῖς λαλεῖν· ἀλλὰ ὑποτασσέσθωσαν, καθὼς καὶ ὁ νόμος λέγει.

records.literal_gloss: The women in the churches let be silent, not for it is permitted to them to speak; but let them be subject, just as also the law says.

en.L: Let the women be silent in the churches, for it is not permitted for them to speak; but let them be subject, just as the law also says.
en.B: In the churches the women are to keep silent. They are not permitted to speak; instead they are to be subject, as the law also says.
en.R: In the church meetings the women must be silent. They are not allowed to speak. Instead, they must be submissive, as the law also says.

fr.L: Que les femmes se taisent dans les églises, car il ne leur est pas permis de parler ; mais qu’elles soient soumises, comme le dit aussi la loi.
fr.B: Dans les églises, les femmes doivent se taire. Il ne leur est pas permis de parler ; elles doivent au contraire être soumises, comme le dit aussi la loi.
fr.R: Pendant les réunions de l’église, les femmes doivent se taire. Elles n’ont pas le droit de parler. Elles doivent au contraire se soumettre, comme le dit aussi la loi.

es.L: Las mujeres callen en las iglesias, porque no les está permitido hablar; sino que estén sujetas, como también dice la ley.
es.B: En las iglesias, las mujeres deben guardar silencio. No se les permite hablar; más bien, deben estar sujetas, como también dice la ley.
es.R: En las reuniones de la iglesia, las mujeres deben callar. No se les permite hablar. Al contrario, deben ser sumisas, como también dice la ley.

sw.L: Wanawake na wanyamaze katika makanisa, kwa maana hawaruhusiwi kusema; bali wajitiishe, kama vile sheria nayo inavyosema.
sw.B: Katika makanisa wanawake wanyamaze. Hawaruhusiwi kusema; badala yake wajitiishe, kama sheria nayo inavyosema.
sw.R: Katika mikutano ya kanisa wanawake wanapaswa kunyamaza. Hawaruhusiwi kusema. Badala yake wanapaswa kuwa watiifu, kama sheria nayo inavyosema.

vi.L: Các người nữ hãy im lặng trong các Hội Thánh, vì họ không được phép nói; nhưng hãy thuận phục, như luật pháp cũng nói.

vi.R: Trong các buổi nhóm của Hội Thánh, phụ nữ phải im lặng. Họ không được phép nói. Thay vào đó, họ phải vâng phục, như luật pháp cũng nói.

ko.L: 여자들은 교회들에서 잠잠하십시오. 그들에게는 말하는 것이 허락되지 않습니다. 율법도 말하는 것처럼 그들은 복종하십시오.
ko.B: 여자들은 교회들에서 잠잠히 있으십시오. 그들에게는 말하는 것이 허락되지 않습니다. 율법도 말하듯이 그들은 복종해야 합니다.
ko.R: 교회 모임에서 여자들은 잠잠히 있어야 합니다. 그들에게는 말하는 것이 허락되지 않습니다. 율법도 말하듯이 그들은 복종해야 합니다.

pt.L: As mulheres fiquem em silêncio nas igrejas, pois não lhes é permitido falar; mas estejam sujeitas, como também a Lei diz.
pt.B: Nas igrejas, as mulheres devem ficar em silêncio. Não lhes é permitido falar; em vez disso, devem estar sujeitas, como também diz a Lei.
pt.R: Nas reuniões da igreja, as mulheres devem ficar em silêncio. Elas não têm permissão para falar. Em vez disso, devem ser submissas, como a Lei também diz.

decisions.choice: verses 34-35 stand here, after verse 33, as the SBLGNT prints them
alternatives: the verses stand after verse 40, as in some manuscripts
the verses were not written by Paul but added to the letter later
decisions.reason: Verses 34-35 are found in every known manuscript of the letter, but not all in the same place: some manuscripts, Greek and Latin witnesses of the so-called Western text, place them after verse 40, at the end of the chapter. Because of this displacement, some scholars think the verses began as a note in the margin that copyists later put into the text at two different points, and so question whether Paul wrote them; others hold that he did and that the verses were moved by copyists. The SBLGNT prints them here, and this translation follows it. Reviewers must check the evidence against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: the women: women in the gathering, in general
alternatives: wives: married women, whose husbands are mentioned in verse 35
decisions.reason: γυναῖκες means both 'women' and 'wives'. As in 11:3-16, the general sense is chosen, since the sentence speaks of women in the churches. But verse 35 tells them to ask 'their own husbands', so married women are at least the main ones in view, and some read 'wives' throughout. In that world most adult women were married.

decisions.choice: a particular kind of speaking that disturbed the gathering, most likely asking questions aloud during the meeting, not every kind of speech
alternatives: speaking in the weighing of prophecies (verse 29), perhaps judging what one's own husband had prophesied
a saying of some in Corinth, which Paul quotes in verses 34-35 and rejects in verse 36
a general rule that women are not to speak at all when the church meets
decisions.reason: In 11:5 Paul takes it for granted that women pray and prophesy aloud when the church meets, and tells them only how to be dressed when they do. So the silence here is probably not total. The context is about order: the speaker in tongues is to be silent when there is no interpreter (verse 28), and a prophet when another receives a revelation (verse 30). Verse 35 speaks of wanting to learn and of asking at home, which points to questions. Some connect the verse with the weighing of prophecies just mentioned (verse 29). Some read verses 34-35 as a Corinthian view that Paul quotes and answers in verse 36, though nothing in the Greek marks them as a quotation. Others take them as a general rule for worship. λαλεῖν is the ordinary verb 'speak', used throughout the chapter for tongues and prophecy as well as for ordinary talk, so the word itself does not decide.

decisions.choice: the law: Paul does not say which law, and what is meant is not clear
alternatives: the account of creation in Genesis 2, as in 11:8-9
Genesis 3:16, where the husband rules over the wife
the teaching of the Old Testament in general
Jewish or Roman law and custom of the time
decisions.reason: No passage of the Old Testament commands women to be silent. 'As the law also says' appeals to νόμος, which Paul uses of the law of Moses and, in verse 21, of the Scriptures as a whole. He may mean the order of creation (11:8-9), or Genesis 3:16, or the general teaching of Scripture; others think of Jewish tradition or of the customs of the time. Paul does not say.

decisions.choice: be subject: take their place in an order under another; to whom is not stated
alternatives: subject to the order of the gathering, as the spirits of prophets are subject to prophets (verse 32)
decisions.reason: ὑποτασσέσθωσαν is the same verb as in verse 32. It means to put oneself under, to take one's place in an order; the Greek names no one to whom the women are subject. Verse 35 suggests their husbands; verse 32 suggests the orderly conduct of the meeting.

decisions.choice: it is not permitted: the practice of the churches does not allow it
decisions.reason: ἐπιτρέπεται is passive and does not say who forbids. The appeal to 'all the churches' just before (verse 33) and to 'the law' points to a practice held in common.

decisions.choice: be silent (L, R); keep silent (B)
decisions.reason: The same English as for the same verb in verses 28 and 30, so that readers can compare them.

decisions.choice: be subject (L, B); be submissive (R)
decisions.reason: 'Be subject' is the same English as in verse 32, so the link is visible; Readable says 'submissive', a plainer word for the same thing. No level says to whom (m5).

decisions.choice: women
decisions.reason: As in 11:3-16 (m2); the footnote gives 'wives'.

decisions.choice: In the church meetings
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that 'the churches' are the gatherings of believers, not buildings.

decisions.choice: la loi, lowercase (against "la Loi" for the Scriptures in 14:21)
decisions.reason: Paul does not say which law he means, and what is meant is not clear (m4). The capital would decide that it is the Law of Moses; the lowercase leaves the question open, as the meaning decision does.

decisions.choice: estar sujetas (L, B); ser sumisas (R)
decisions.reason: The verb means to take one's place in an order under another, without saying under whom (m5). "Estar sujetas" keeps the same verb as "los espíritus de los profetas están sujetos" in verse 32; Readable "ser sumisas" follows the English "be submissive".

decisions.choice: wajitiishe (L, B); wawe watiifu (R)
decisions.reason: "Kujitiisha" (put oneself under) is taking one's place in an order, and like the Greek it does not say under whom (meaning decision); "kutii" (obey) would say more. Readable "watiifu" (submissive) follows the English Readable.

decisions.choice: "các người nữ" (L), "phụ nữ" (B, R); "im lặng" at every level, as for the speakers of 14:28 and 14:30; "thuận phục" (L, B), "vâng phục" (R)
decisions.reason: "Im lặng" is the word of verses 28 and 30, so the reader can see that Paul uses the same verb for the speaker in tongues, the prophet and the women; m3 and m5 give the debated sense. "Thuận phục" is the word of the Vietnamese 1 Timothy 2:11.

decisions.choice: "여자들" (not "아내들"); "잠잠하다"; "복종하다" with no one named to whom
decisions.reason: The meaning decisions read the women in general, uncertain and footnoted, and note that the Greek names no one to whom they are to be subject; Korean does not add "to their husbands". The verb is "복종하다", the word of verse 32 for the prophets' spirits, as the Greek has the same verb.

decisions.choice: estejam sujeitas (L), devem estar sujeitas (B); devem ser submissas (R)
decisions.reason: "Sujeito" is the word used for the prophets' spirits in verse 32, so the link is visible, as in the English; Readable says "submissas", the plainer word. No level says to whom (m5).

source.text: εἰ δέ τι μαθεῖν θέλουσιν, ἐν οἴκῳ τοὺς ἰδίους ἄνδρας ἐπερωτάτωσαν, αἰσχρὸν γάρ ἐστιν γυναικὶ λαλεῖν ἐν ἐκκλησίᾳ.

records.literal_gloss: If but something to learn they want, at home the own husbands let them ask, shameful for it is for a woman to speak in church.

en.L: And if they want to learn something, let them question their own husbands at home; for it is shameful for a woman to speak in church.
en.B: If there is something they wish to learn, they are to put their questions to their own husbands at home. It is shameful for a woman to speak when the church meets.
en.R: If they want to learn about something, they should ask their own husbands when they are at home. It is shameful for a woman to speak in a church meeting.

fr.L: Et si elles veulent apprendre quelque chose, qu’elles interrogent leurs propres maris à la maison ; car il est honteux pour une femme de parler dans l’église.
fr.B: S’il y a quelque chose qu’elles veulent apprendre, qu’elles posent leurs questions à leur propre mari, à la maison. Car il est honteux pour une femme de parler quand l’église est réunie.
fr.R: Si elles veulent apprendre quelque chose, elles doivent poser la question à leur mari quand elles sont à la maison. Car il est honteux pour une femme de parler pendant une réunion de l’église.

es.L: Y si quieren aprender algo, que pregunten en casa a sus propios maridos; porque es vergonzoso para una mujer hablar en [la] iglesia.
es.B: Si desean aprender algo, que hagan sus preguntas a sus propios maridos en casa. Es vergonzoso que una mujer hable cuando la iglesia se reúne.
es.R: Si quieren saber algo, deben preguntarles a sus propios esposos cuando estén en casa. Es vergonzoso que una mujer hable en una reunión de la iglesia.

sw.L: Na ikiwa wanataka kujifunza jambo, na wawaulize waume zao wenyewe nyumbani; kwa maana ni aibu kwa mwanamke kusema katika kanisa.
sw.B: Ikiwa kuna jambo wanalotaka kujifunza, wawaulize waume zao wenyewe nyumbani. Ni aibu kwa mwanamke kusema kanisa linapokutana.
sw.R: Ikiwa wanataka kujifunza kuhusu jambo fulani, wawaulize waume zao wenyewe wanapokuwa nyumbani. Ni aibu kwa mwanamke kusema katika mkutano wa kanisa.

vi.L: Và nếu họ muốn học điều gì, hãy hỏi chồng mình ở nhà; vì người nữ nói trong Hội Thánh là điều đáng hổ thẹn.
vi.B: Nếu có điều gì họ muốn học, thì hãy hỏi chồng mình ở nhà. Người phụ nữ nói khi Hội Thánh nhóm họp là điều đáng hổ thẹn.
vi.R: Nếu muốn biết thêm về điều gì, họ nên hỏi chồng mình khi ở nhà. Người phụ nữ nói trong buổi nhóm Hội Thánh là điều đáng xấu hổ.

ko.L: 그들이 무엇을 배우고 싶으면 집에서 자기 남편들에게 물어보십시오. 여자가 교회에서 말하는 것은 부끄러운 일이기 때문입니다.
ko.B: 그들이 배우고 싶은 것이 있으면, 집에서 자기 남편에게 물어보십시오. 여자가 교회 모임에서 말하는 것은 부끄러운 일입니다.
ko.R: 그들이 무엇에 대해 배우고 싶으면, 집에 있을 때 자기 남편에게 물어보아야 합니다. 여자가 교회 모임에서 말하는 것은 부끄러운 일입니다.

pt.L: E, se querem aprender alguma coisa, perguntem em casa aos próprios maridos; pois é vergonhoso para uma mulher falar na igreja.
pt.B: Se há alguma coisa que elas desejam aprender, devem fazer as suas perguntas aos próprios maridos em casa. É vergonhoso para uma mulher falar quando a igreja está reunida.
pt.R: Se elas querem aprender alguma coisa, devem perguntar aos próprios maridos quando estiverem em casa. É vergonhoso para uma mulher falar numa reunião da igreja.

decisions.choice: the verse stands here, with verse 34, as the SBLGNT prints it
alternatives: the verse stands after verse 40, as in some manuscripts
decisions.reason: This verse moves with verse 34: the manuscripts that place verse 34 after verse 40 place this verse there too. See the text decision on verse 34. Reviewers must check the evidence against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: their own husbands: the women in view are, at least mainly, married
decisions.reason: τοὺς ἰδίους ἄνδρας is 'their own men', which here means husbands, as in 7:2 ('her own husband'). Paul does not say what unmarried women or widows, who had no husband to ask, should do (7:8, 34).

decisions.choice: if they want to learn: the speaking in view is tied to learning and asking
decisions.reason: Paul assumes that the women want to learn and gives them a place to do it. This is one reason the speaking forbidden in verse 34 is read as asking questions (decision m3 there).

decisions.choice: shameful: bringing dishonor in the eyes of others
decisions.reason: αἰσχρὸν is the word used in 11:6 of a woman's cropped or shaved head. In the Greek and Roman world it was widely thought improper for a married woman to speak with men outside her family in public; Paul appeals to that sense of shame.

decisions.choice: a woman: the same word as 'the women' in verse 34
decisions.reason: As in verse 34 (m2 there).

decisions.choice: when the church meets (B); in a church meeting (R)
decisions.reason: ἐν ἐκκλησίᾳ has no article: the church as it meets, not a building. Literal keeps 'in church'.

decisions.choice: put their questions to
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the sense of the verb, which is asking questions.

decisions.choice: maridos (L, B); esposos (R)
decisions.reason: As in 7:2-4: "marido" at Literal and Balanced, "esposo" at Readable. The Greek word for "men" here means husbands (m2).

source.text: ἢ ἀφ’ ὑμῶν ὁ λόγος τοῦ θεοῦ ἐξῆλθεν, ἢ εἰς ὑμᾶς μόνους κατήντησεν;

records.literal_gloss: Or from you the word of the God went out, or to you alone did it reach?

en.L: Or did the word of God go out from you, or did it reach you alone?
en.B: Or did God's word go out from you? Has it come to you and no one else?
en.R: Do you think God's message began with you? Do you think you are the only people who have received it?

fr.L: Ou bien est-ce de chez vous que la parole de Dieu est sortie, ou est-ce à vous seuls qu’elle est parvenue ?
fr.B: La parole de Dieu est-elle partie de chez vous ? Est-elle venue jusqu’à vous seuls, et à personne d’autre ?
fr.R: Pensez-vous que le message de Dieu a commencé avec vous ? Pensez-vous que vous êtes les seuls à l’avoir reçu ?

es.L: ¿O salió de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} la palabra de Dios, o llegó solo a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}?
es.B: ¿Acaso salió de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} la palabra de Dios? ¿Ha llegado a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} y a nadie más?
es.R: ¿{{plural_you:Creen|Creéis}} que el mensaje de Dios comenzó con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}? ¿{{plural_you:Creen|Creéis}} que {{plural_you:son|sois}} los únicos que lo han recibido?

sw.L: Au je, neno la Mungu lilitoka kwenu, au liliwafikia ninyi peke yenu?
sw.B: Au je, neno la Mungu lilianzia kwenu? Je, limewafikia ninyi tu, na si mtu mwingine?
sw.R: Je, mnadhani ujumbe wa Mungu ulianza kwenu? Je, mnadhani ninyi ndio watu pekee mlioupokea?

vi.L: Hay là lời của Đức Chúa Trời đã ra từ anh chị em, hoặc chỉ đến với một mình anh chị em thôi sao?
vi.B: Hay là lời Đức Chúa Trời đã khởi đầu từ anh chị em? Có phải lời ấy chỉ đến với anh chị em mà không đến với ai khác sao?
vi.R: Anh chị em nghĩ rằng sứ điệp của Đức Chúa Trời đã bắt đầu từ anh chị em sao? Anh chị em nghĩ rằng chỉ có anh chị em là những người đã nhận được sứ điệp ấy sao?

ko.L: 아니면 하나님의 말씀이 여러분에게서 나왔습니까? 아니면 여러분에게만 이르렀습니까?
ko.B: 하나님의 말씀이 여러분에게서 시작되었다는 말입니까? 그 말씀이 여러분에게만 왔다는 말입니까?
ko.R: 여러분은 하나님의 말씀이 여러분에게서 시작되었다고 생각합니까? 그 말씀을 받은 사람이 여러분뿐이라고 생각합니까?

pt.L: Ou foi de vocês que a palavra de Deus saiu, ou só a vocês ela chegou?
pt.B: Ou será que a palavra de Deus saiu de vocês? Será que ela chegou só a vocês e a mais ninguém?
pt.R: Vocês acham que a mensagem de Deus começou com vocês? Vocês acham que são as únicas pessoas que a receberam?

decisions.choice: rhetorical questions that expect the answer no
decisions.reason: The two questions, each opened by ἢ ('or'), mean that the word of God did not start in Corinth, and that the Corinthians are not its only receivers. They should follow what all the churches do (verse 33; 11:16).

decisions.choice: you alone: the whole church at Corinth is addressed
alternatives: Paul answers a Corinthian saying in verses 34-35, as if to say: 'What! Did the word of God come from you?'
decisions.reason: μόνους is masculine plural, the form used for a mixed group, so Paul speaks to the church as a whole, and probably to all who think they may set their own rules (verse 37). Those who read verses 34-35 as a Corinthian saying take ἢ as an exclamation rejecting it; the word can introduce such a reply, but nothing marks the verses before it as a quotation.

decisions.choice: the word of God: the message of the gospel
decisions.reason: ὁ λόγος τοῦ θεοῦ is the gospel God has spoken, which reached Corinth through Paul (Acts 18:1-11; 2 Corinthians 10:14).

decisions.choice: Do you think
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that the questions challenge what the Corinthians assume (m1).

decisions.choice: God's message
decisions.reason: Readable uses a plainer word for the same thing (m3).

source.text: Εἴ τις δοκεῖ προφήτης εἶναι ἢ πνευματικός, ἐπιγινωσκέτω ἃ γράφω ὑμῖν ὅτι κυρίου ἐστὶν·

records.literal_gloss: If anyone thinks a prophet to be or spiritual, let him recognize [the things] which I write to you, that of [the] Lord it is;

en.L: If anyone thinks {{gender:they are|he is}} a prophet or spiritual, let {{gender:them|him}} recognize that the things I write to you are of [the] Lord.
en.B: If anyone thinks {{gender:they are|he is}} a prophet or spiritual, {{gender:they|he}} should recognize that what I am writing to you comes from the Lord.
en.R: Some of you may think you are prophets or have special gifts from the Spirit. If so, you should see that what I am writing to you comes from the Lord.

fr.L: Si quelqu’un pense être prophète ou spirituel, qu’il reconnaisse que ce que je vous écris est du Seigneur.
fr.B: Si quelqu’un pense être prophète ou spirituel, il doit reconnaître que ce que je vous écris vient du Seigneur.
fr.R: Certains d’entre vous pensent peut-être être prophètes, ou avoir des dons particuliers de l’Esprit. Si c’est le cas, vous devez comprendre que ce que je vous écris vient du Seigneur.

es.L: Si alguno cree ser profeta o espiritual, reconozca que lo que {{plural_you:les|os}} escribo es del Señor.
es.B: Si alguien se considera profeta o persona espiritual, debe reconocer que lo que {{plural_you:les|os}} escribo viene del Señor.
es.R: Puede que algunos de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} {{plural_you:piensen|penséis}} que son profetas o que tienen dones especiales del Espíritu. Si es así, deben ver que lo que {{plural_you:les|os}} escribo viene del Señor.

sw.L: Mtu yeyote akidhani kwamba yeye ni nabii au wa kiroho, na atambue kwamba mambo ninayowaandikia ni ya Bwana.
sw.B: Mtu yeyote akidhani kwamba yeye ni nabii au mtu wa kiroho, anapaswa kutambua kwamba ninayowaandikia yanatoka kwa Bwana.
sw.R: Baadhi yenu mnaweza kudhani kwamba ninyi ni manabii au mna karama maalum kutoka kwa Roho. Ikiwa ndivyo, mnapaswa kuona kwamba ninayowaandikia yanatoka kwa Bwana.

vi.L: Nếu ai nghĩ mình là nhà tiên tri hay là người thuộc linh, thì hãy nhận biết rằng những điều tôi viết cho anh chị em là [mệnh lệnh] của Chúa.
vi.B: Nếu ai nghĩ mình là nhà tiên tri hay là người thuộc linh, thì người ấy phải nhận biết rằng những gì tôi viết cho anh chị em đến từ Chúa.
vi.R: Có thể có người trong anh chị em nghĩ rằng mình là nhà tiên tri hay có những ân tứ đặc biệt từ Thánh Linh. Nếu vậy, anh chị em phải thấy rằng những gì tôi đang viết cho anh chị em đến từ Chúa.

ko.L: 누구든지 자기가 예언자이거나 영적인 사람이라고 생각한다면, 내가 여러분에게 쓰는 것이 주님의 [명령]이라는 것을 인정하십시오.
ko.B: 누구든지 자기가 예언자이거나 성령의 사람이라고 생각한다면, 내가 여러분에게 쓰는 이 말이 주님께로부터 온 것이라는 것을 인정해야 합니다.
ko.R: 여러분 가운데 어떤 사람은 자기가 예언자이거나 성령께서 주신 특별한 은사를 가졌다고 생각할지도 모릅니다. 그렇다면 내가 여러분에게 쓰는 것이 주님께로부터 온 것임을 알아야 합니다.

pt.L: Se alguém pensa ser profeta ou espiritual, reconheça que as coisas que eu lhes escrevo são do Senhor.
pt.B: Se alguém pensa que é profeta ou espiritual, deve reconhecer que o que estou escrevendo a vocês vem do Senhor.
pt.R: Alguns de vocês podem achar que são profetas ou que têm dons especiais do Espírito. Se for assim, vocês devem perceber que o que estou escrevendo a vocês vem do Senhor.

decisions.choice: what Paul writes 'is of the Lord', as the SBLGNT prints it
alternatives: 'is a command of the Lord', as many manuscripts read
'are commands of the Lord', as other manuscripts read
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts add the word for 'command' after 'of the Lord', some in the singular and some in the plural. The SBLGNT follows manuscripts that lack it, and the different forms of the addition suggest that copyists supplied it to complete the phrase. The sense is much the same: what Paul writes carries the Lord's authority. Reviewers must check the evidence against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: spiritual: a person of the Spirit, gifted by the Spirit
decisions.reason: πνευματικός is the word of 2:15 and 3:1. Some in Corinth seem to have claimed to be spiritual because of their gifts; Paul says that someone truly spiritual will recognize his instruction.

decisions.choice: thinks: considers oneself, perhaps claims to be
decisions.reason: δοκεῖ means to think or seem; here it is what people think of themselves (3:18; 8:2).

decisions.choice: the Lord: Jesus Christ
decisions.reason: As often in this letter, κυρίου alone means the Lord Jesus (7:10, 25).

decisions.choice: have special gifts from the Spirit
decisions.reason: Readable says what being spiritual means here (m2).

decisions.choice: Some of you may think you are
decisions.reason: Readable speaks directly to the readers, as the next words do ('what I am writing to you').

decisions.choice: "주님의 [명령]" (L); "주님께로부터 온 것" (B, R)
alternatives: "주님의 명령" without brackets at every level
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT has only "of the Lord", without the word "command" that many manuscripts add; Literal brackets the noun Korean needs.

source.text: εἰ δέ τις ἀγνοεῖ, ἀγνοεῖται.

records.literal_gloss: If but anyone does not recognize, he is not recognized.

en.L: But if anyone does not recognize [this], {{gender:they are|he is}} not recognized.
en.B: Anyone who refuses to recognize this is not recognized either.
en.R: If anyone refuses to recognize this, God does not recognize that person either.

fr.L: Mais si quelqu’un ne reconnaît pas [cela], il n’est pas reconnu.
fr.B: Celui qui refuse de le reconnaître n’est pas reconnu non plus.
fr.R: Si quelqu’un refuse de reconnaître cela, Dieu ne le reconnaît pas non plus.

es.L: Pero si alguno no [lo] reconoce, no es reconocido.
es.B: Quien se niegue a reconocerlo tampoco es reconocido.
es.R: Si alguien se niega a reconocer esto, Dios tampoco reconoce a esa persona.

sw.L: Lakini mtu yeyote asipotambua [hili], yeye hatambuliwi.
sw.B: Mtu yeyote anayekataa kutambua jambo hili, yeye pia hatambuliwi.
sw.R: Ikiwa mtu yeyote anakataa kutambua jambo hili, Mungu naye hamtambui mtu huyo.

vi.L: Nhưng nếu ai không nhận biết [điều này], thì người ấy không được nhận biết.
vi.B: Ai không chịu nhận biết điều này thì cũng sẽ không được nhận biết.
vi.R: Nếu ai không chịu nhận biết điều này, thì Đức Chúa Trời cũng không nhận biết người ấy.

ko.L: 누구든지 [이것을] 인정하지 않으면, 그도 인정을 받지 못합니다.
ko.B: 누구든지 이것을 인정하지 않는 사람은 그 자신도 인정을 받지 못합니다.
ko.R: 누구든지 이것을 인정하지 않으면, 하나님께서도 그 사람을 인정하지 않으실 것입니다.

pt.L: Mas, se alguém não [o] reconhece, não é reconhecido.
pt.B: Quem se recusa a reconhecer isso também não é reconhecido.
pt.R: Se alguém se recusa a reconhecer isso, Deus também não reconhece essa pessoa.

decisions.choice: is not recognized: a statement, as the SBLGNT prints it
alternatives: 'let him not recognize it', a command, as other manuscripts read
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts have a command form of the same verb, 'let him be ignorant', meaning that Paul will leave such a person to their ignorance. Others, which the SBLGNT follows, have the passive statement. The two forms differ by only a few letters. Reviewers must check the evidence against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: is not recognized: by God
alternatives: is not to be recognized by the church as a prophet or spiritual person
decisions.reason: ἀγνοεῖται is passive, and Paul often leaves God unnamed as the one who acts. In 8:3 the one who loves God is known by him; here the one who does not acknowledge the Lord's word is not acknowledged. Some take it as a word to the church: do not accept such a person's claim to be a prophet.

decisions.choice: a play on one verb: whoever does not recognize is not recognized
decisions.reason: ἀγνοεῖ and ἀγνοεῖται are the active and passive of the same verb, which means not to know or not to acknowledge; the consequence matches the fault, and it answers 'let him recognize' in verse 37.

decisions.choice: God does not recognize that person
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one who does not recognize (m2); since that is uncertain, it is marked for reviewers.

decisions.choice: refuses to recognize
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable show that the failure is a refusal, the opposite of 'recognize' in verse 37 (m3).

decisions.choice: kutambua ... hatambuliwi
decisions.reason: One verb, "kutambua" (recognize), in the active and the passive, keeps Paul's play on words (meaning decision) at every level; Readable names God as the one who does not recognize, as the English Readable.

decisions.choice: "인정하다 ... 인정을 받다" for the play on one verb
decisions.reason: The meaning decision notes that the active and passive of the same verb make a play on words; Korean keeps it with one verb, "인정하다", and Readable names God, as the English does.

source.text: ὥστε, ἀδελφοί μου, ζηλοῦτε τὸ προφητεύειν, καὶ τὸ λαλεῖν μὴ κωλύετε γλώσσαις·

records.literal_gloss: So then, brothers of me, be zealous for the to prophesy, and the to speak do not forbid in tongues;

en.L: So then, my {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, be zealous to prophesy, and do not forbid speaking in tongues.
en.B: So then, my {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, set your hearts on prophesying, and do not stop anyone from speaking in tongues.
en.R: So, my {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, try hard to prophesy. And do not stop people from speaking in tongues.

fr.L: Ainsi donc, mes {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}, aspirez à prophétiser, et n’empêchez pas de parler en langues.
fr.B: Ainsi donc, mes {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}, désirez vivement prophétiser, et n’empêchez personne de parler en langues.
fr.R: Alors, mes {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}, cherchez de tout votre cœur à prophétiser. Et n’empêchez pas les gens de parler en langues.

es.L: Así que, hermanos míos, {{plural_you:procuren con celo|procurad con celo}} profetizar, y no {{plural_you:impidan|impidáis}} el hablar en lenguas.
es.B: Así pues, hermanos míos, {{plural_you:anhelen|anhelad}} profetizar, y no {{plural_you:impidan|impidáis}} a nadie hablar en lenguas.
es.R: Así que, hermanos míos, {{plural_you:procuren|procurad}} profetizar. Y no {{plural_you:impidan|impidáis}} que la gente hable en lenguas.

sw.L: Basi, ndugu zangu, kuweni na shauku ya kutabiri, wala msikataze kunena kwa lugha.
sw.B: Basi, ndugu zangu, tamanini sana kutabiri, wala msimzuie mtu kunena kwa lugha.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo, ndugu zangu, jitahidini kutabiri. Na msiwazuie watu kunena kwa lugha.

vi.L: Vậy, thưa {{gender:anh chị em|anh em}} của tôi, hãy khao khát nói tiên tri, và đừng ngăn cấm việc nói tiếng lạ.
vi.B: Vậy, thưa {{gender:anh chị em|anh em}} của tôi, hãy hết lòng ước ao nói tiên tri, và đừng ngăn cản ai nói tiếng lạ.
vi.R: Vậy, thưa {{gender:anh chị em|anh em}} của tôi, hãy cố gắng nói tiên tri. Và đừng ngăn cản người khác nói tiếng lạ.

ko.L: 그러므로 나의 {{gender:형제자매|형제}} 여러분, 예언하기를 열심히 구하고, 방언으로 말하는 것을 금하지 마십시오.
ko.B: 그러므로 나의 {{gender:형제자매|형제}} 여러분, 예언하기를 간절히 사모하고, 방언으로 말하는 것을 막지 마십시오.
ko.R: 그러니 나의 {{gender:형제자매|형제}} 여러분, 예언하려고 힘쓰십시오. 그리고 사람들이 방언으로 말하는 것을 막지 마십시오.

pt.L: Assim, meus {{gender:irmãos e irmãs|irmãos}}, sejam zelosos por profetizar e não proíbam o falar em línguas.
pt.B: Assim, meus {{gender:irmãos e irmãs|irmãos}}, desejem de todo o coração profetizar e não impeçam ninguém de falar em línguas.
pt.R: Por isso, meus {{gender:irmãos e irmãs|irmãos}}, esforcem-se para profetizar. E não impeçam as pessoas de falar em línguas.

decisions.choice: so then: the conclusion of the chapter
decisions.reason: ὥστε sums up chapters 12-14 in two commands.

decisions.choice: be zealous for: seek eagerly, as in 12:31 and 14:1
decisions.reason: ζηλοῦτε is the verb of 12:31 and 14:1.

decisions.choice: do not forbid speaking in tongues: tongues have their place, within the order of verses 27-28
decisions.reason: Paul has ranked prophecy higher, but he does not let the church shut out tongues; interpreted and in turn, they too build up the church (verse 5).

decisions.choice: set your hearts on (B); try hard to (R)
decisions.reason: As in 12:31 and 14:1.

source.text: πάντα δὲ εὐσχημόνως καὶ κατὰ τάξιν γινέσθω.

records.literal_gloss: All things but fittingly and according to order let be done.

en.L: But let all things be done fittingly and according to order.
en.B: But let everything be done properly and in good order.
en.R: But make sure that everything is done properly, in an orderly way.

fr.L: Mais que tout se fasse convenablement et selon l’ordre.
fr.B: Mais que tout se fasse comme il convient et avec ordre.
fr.R: Mais veillez à ce que tout se fasse correctement, dans l’ordre.

es.L: Pero hágase todo decentemente y con orden.
es.B: Pero que todo se haga como es debido y con buen orden.
es.R: Pero {{plural_you:asegúrense|aseguraos}} de que todo se haga como es debido, de manera ordenada.

sw.L: Lakini mambo yote na yafanyike kwa kufaa na kwa utaratibu.
sw.B: Lakini kila kitu kifanyike ipasavyo na kwa utaratibu mzuri.
sw.R: Lakini hakikisheni kwamba kila kitu kinafanyika ipasavyo, kwa utaratibu.

vi.L: Nhưng mọi sự hãy được làm cách đứng đắn và theo trật tự.
vi.B: Nhưng hãy làm mọi việc cách đứng đắn và có trật tự.
vi.R: Nhưng hãy làm sao cho mọi việc đều được thực hiện cách đứng đắn và có thứ tự.

ko.L: 모든 것을 품위 있게, 질서를 따라 하십시오.
ko.B: 모든 것을 적절하고 질서 있게 하십시오.
ko.R: 모든 일을 바르게, 질서 있게 하도록 하십시오.

pt.L: Mas tudo seja feito com decoro e segundo a ordem.
pt.B: Mas que tudo seja feito de maneira apropriada e em boa ordem.
pt.R: Mas cuidem para que tudo seja feito de modo apropriado e organizado.

decisions.choice: fittingly: in a way that is proper and becoming
decisions.reason: εὐσχημόνως describes what is seemly and fitting. Its root is the word for the 'presentable' parts of the body in 12:23-24, and it is used in Romans 13:13 and 1 Thessalonians 4:12 of conduct that is fitting before others.

decisions.choice: according to order: in proper sequence, each in turn
decisions.reason: τάξιν is an ordered arrangement, used of priests serving in turn (Luke 1:8). It sums up verses 27-33: one at a time, in turn, as befits the God of peace, not of disorder.

decisions.choice: properly
decisions.reason: 'Decently' now suggests only modesty; the Greek word means what is fitting.

decisions.choice: com decoro
decisions.reason: Literal uses the word of 12:23-24 ("indecorosos ... decoro ... decorosos"), since the Greek adverb comes from the same root (m1); Balanced and Readable say "apropriado".
